panels.description:
Average number of active database connections (CloudWatch).
Sudden growth may indicate connection leaks or traffic spikes.
panels.title: RDS Connections

panels.description:
Average number of disk I/O requests waiting in queue (CloudWatch).
A sustained queue depth > 1 indicates disk contention and I/O bottlenecks.
panels.title: RDS Disk Queue Depth

panels.description:
Amount of available RAM for the RDS instance (CloudWatch).
Low freeable memory may lead to swapping and performance degradation.
panels.title: RDS Freeable Memory

panels.description:
Average number of read I/O operations per second for the RDS instance (CloudWatch).
Shows how intensively the database reads data from disk.
Sustained high Read IOPS may indicate disk-bound workloads, inefficient queries, or missing indexes.
Thresholds are based on the IOPS limits of the underlying storage type.
panels.title: RDS Read IOPS

panels.description:
Average CPU utilization of the RDS instance (CloudWatch).
Sustained high CPU may cause slow queries and increased latency.
panels.title: RDS CPU Utilization

panels.description:
RabbitMQ
Total number of messages across all queuesVisualization
panels.title: Queue Depth (Messages)

panels.description:
RabbitMQ / AmazonMQ

Total number of active client connections to the broker.
Helps detect connection leaks, retry storms, or client crashes.
panels.title: RabbitMQ – Connections

panels.description:
RabbitMQ / AmazonMQ

Total number of active consumers connected to the broker.
Used to detect consumer outages, crashes, or scaling issues.

If value drops to 0 — messages will accumulate and queues will grow.
panels.title: RabbitMQ – Consumer Count

panels.description:
RabbitMQ / AmazonMQ

Inbound and outbound network throughput of the broker.
Acts as a CPU-proxy metric for AmazonMQ.

High sustained traffic may indicate broker saturation,
routing pressure, or insufficient instance size.
panels.title: RabbitMQ – Network Throughput

panels.description:
RabbitMQ / AmazonMQ
Average number of messages per consumer.
Calculated as:
total MessageCount / ConsumerCount (with clamp to avoid division by zero).
Helps detect consumer saturation, lag, or outages.
panels.title: RabbitMQ – Consumers & Processing

panels.description:
RabbitMQ
Incoming messages per second (calculated from MessageCount)
panels.title: Message Inflow Rate (msg/sec) RabbitMQ

panels.description:
Shows the current number of keys stored in Redis / ElastiCache.
A sudden drop to zero may indicate cache flush or node restart.
Constant growth may indicate missing TTL or memory leak.
panels.title: Redis Keys Count (Current Items)

panels.description:
Percentage of requests served from cache (Redis / Memcached).
High values indicate effective caching.
Low values mean frequent cache misses and increased load on backend services (e.g. RDS).
panels.title: Query (Redis / Memcached)

panels.description:
Number of cache evictions per second.
Evictions indicate that the cache is running out of memory.
Frequent evictions reduce cache efficiency and increase database load.
panels.title: Cache Evictions (ops/sec)

panels.description:
Current number of active client connections to Redis / Memcached.
A high number of connections may indicate connection leaks,
inefficient pooling, or insufficient cache node sizing.
panels.title: Current Connections (Redis / Memcached)

panels.description:
Amount of memory currently used by Redis / Memcached.
High memory usage may lead to evictions and cache inefficiency.
panels.title: Cache Memory Used ( Redis / Memcached)

panels.description:
Average CPU utilization of Redis / Memcached nodes.

High CPU usage may indicate insufficient node size,
inefficient commands, or excessive client load.
panels.title: Cache CPU Utilization

panels.description:
Inbound and outbound network traffic per EC2 instance.
Calculated from AWS NetworkIn / NetworkOut metrics via CloudWatch (YACE).
Displayed as bits per second (bps).

Used to detect traffic spikes, retry storms,
network saturation, and correlate with CPU / broker load.
panels.title: EC2 – Network Throughput (IN / OUT)

panels.description:
Actual memory usage based on MemAvailable.
Includes cache and reclaimable memory.
Critical when >85%.
panels.title: EC2 – Memory Usage

panels.description:
CPU utilization per EC2 instance.
Used to detect CPU saturation, runaway processes
and scaling requirements.
panels.title: EC2 – CPU Utilization

panels.description:
Inbound and outbound network traffic per EC2 instance (CloudWatch).
Calculated from NetworkIn/Out SUM metrics.
panels.title: EC2 Network Bandwidth
